<div class="page-shell">

<header class="masthead">
  <div class="eyebrow">WebR practical</div>
  <h1>Simple linear regression with a polytomous predictor</h1>
  <p>When a categorical predictor has more than two levels, R creates <strong>K − 1</strong> dummy variables. You will fit models, recover group means from the output, and practice choosing a sensible reference level.</p>
</header>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Overview</h2>

A <strong>polytomous</strong> predictor has $K > 2$ categories (for example race with three groups, or education with four levels). Do <strong>not</strong> code these as a single numeric variable 0, 1, 2, 3 unless you truly want to force equal steps between every level.

Instead, R picks one <strong>reference</strong> level and creates one dummy variable for each of the other $K - 1$ levels. Each coefficient is that level's mean <strong>difference vs the reference</strong>.

This practical uses datasets from common R packages:

<ul class="tight-list">
  <li><code>oibiostat::prevend.samp</code> — cognitive test score (<code>RFFT</code>) by education (4 levels)</li>
  <li><code>MASS::birthwt</code> — birth weight (<code>bwt</code>) by mother's race (3 levels)</li>
  <li><code>oibiostat::famuss</code> — strength gain (<code>ndrm.ch</code>) by ACTN3 genotype (3 levels)</li>
</ul>

After answering the questions, <strong>your completion code will be revealed.</strong>

</section>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 1</div>
  <p>A categorical predictor with $K = 4$ levels produces how many dummy coefficients (plus the intercept) in a simple regression?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p0" value="a">4 coefficients plus intercept (one per level).</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p0" value="b">3 coefficients plus intercept ($K - 1$ dummies).</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p0" value="c">1 coefficient plus intercept.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. One level is absorbed into the intercept; the other K−1 levels each get a dummy." data-incorrect="Not quite. With K levels, R uses K−1 dummy variables because one level is the reference."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 2</div>
  <p>Why should you avoid coding education as 0, 1, 2, 3 in a single numeric column?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p1" value="a">It forces every step between neighbouring levels to have the same effect size.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p1" value="b">R cannot read numeric columns.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p1" value="c">It removes the intercept from the model.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Numeric coding assumes equal gaps; dummy coding lets each level have its own mean shift vs reference." data-incorrect="Not quite. The problem is the equal-step assumption, not R's ability to fit the model."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>The equation (four education levels, primary reference)</h2>

<div class="formula-panel">

$$\hat{y} = b_0 + b_1 \cdot \text{lower} + b_2 \cdot \text{higher} + b_3 \cdot \text{university}$$

<ul class="tight-list">
  <li>Each dummy equals 1 only for its own level and 0 otherwise.</li>
  <li>$b_0$ = mean of the <strong>reference</strong> group (primary education).</li>
  <li>Each $b_j$ = that level's mean minus the reference mean.</li>
  <li>To recover a group's mean: add its coefficient to the intercept (reference groups add 0).</li>
</ul>

</div>

</section>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Worked example 1: RFFT score by education (<code>oibiostat::prevend.samp</code>)</h2>

The PREVEND sample includes the Ruff Figural Fluency Test score (<code>RFFT</code>), a measure of executive function, and education coded 0–3. We relabel those codes and set <strong>primary</strong> as the reference.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code — prevend, primary reference</h3>

```{webr-r}
library(oibiostat)
data(prevend.samp)

prevend <- prevend.samp
prevend$education <- factor(
  prevend$Education,
  levels = 0:3,
  labels = c("primary", "lower_secondary", "higher_secondary", "university")
)

mod_edu <- lm(RFFT ~ education, data = prevend)
summary(mod_edu)
```

</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 3</div>
  <p>The intercept is about 40.9. This is the mean RFFT score for which education group?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p2" value="a">Primary education (the reference level).</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p2" value="b">University education.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p2" value="c">The average across all four groups.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. The intercept is always the reference group mean." data-incorrect="Not quite. Look at which level was set as reference when creating the factor."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="c">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 4</div>
  <p>The predicted mean RFFT score for participants with <strong>university</strong> education is approximately:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p3" value="a">44.96 points (the coefficient alone).</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p3" value="b">55.7 points (40.9 + 14.8).</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p3" value="c">85.9 points (40.9 + 45.0).</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. University mean = intercept + educationuniversity ≈ 40.9 + 45.0 ≈ 85.9." data-incorrect="Not quite. Add the university coefficient to the intercept. The coefficient is a difference, not the full mean."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 5</div>
  <p>The coefficient for <code>educationlower_secondary</code> (about +14.8) means:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p4" value="a">Lower secondary participants score 14.8 points in total.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p4" value="b">Lower secondary participants score about 14.8 points <strong>above</strong> the primary group.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p4" value="c">Lower secondary participants score about 14.8 points above the university group.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Every dummy coefficient is vs the reference, not vs other non-reference levels." data-incorrect="Not quite. Each row compares that level to the omitted reference (primary), not to another non-reference level."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Worked example 2: birth weight by race (<code>MASS::birthwt</code>)</h2>

The <code>birthwt</code> data record infant birth weight in grams and mother's race (white, black, other). We label the numeric race codes and set <strong>white</strong> as reference.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code — birthwt, white reference</h3>

```{webr-r}
library(MASS)
data(birthwt)

birthwt$race <- factor(birthwt$race, levels = c(1, 2, 3),
                       labels = c("white", "black", "other"))

mod_race <- lm(bwt ~ race, data = birthwt)
summary(mod_race)
```

</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 6</div>
  <p>With white as reference, the intercept (about 3103 g) is the mean birth weight for:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p5" value="a">White mothers' babies.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p5" value="b">Black mothers' babies.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p5" value="c">All babies combined.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. White is the reference level." data-incorrect="Not quite. The intercept is the reference group mean."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 7</div>
  <p>The <code>raceblack</code> coefficient is about −383 g. The predicted mean birth weight for black mothers' babies is approximately:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p6" value="a">383 g</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p6" value="b">2720 g (3103 − 383)</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p6" value="c">3486 g (3103 + 383)</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Black mean = intercept + raceblack ≈ 3103 − 383 ≈ 2720 g." data-incorrect="Not quite. Add the black coefficient to the intercept. The negative sign means lower than white."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Choosing and changing the reference level</h2>

Which reference you pick is a <strong>reporting choice</strong>. Common strategies:

<ul class="tight-list">
  <li><strong>Natural order</strong> — lowest education level, so effects read as gains up a ladder.</li>
  <li><strong>Clinical control</strong> — placebo or standard care, so every coefficient is a treatment effect.</li>
  <li><strong>Largest group</strong> — can yield tighter confidence intervals because the reference mean is estimated precisely.</li>
</ul>

Relevel <code>birthwt</code> so <strong>black</strong> is the reference and compare the output.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code — relevel race to black reference</h3>

```{webr-r}
birthwt_black_ref <- birthwt
birthwt_black_ref$race <- factor(birthwt_black_ref$race,
                                 levels = c("black", "white", "other"))

mod_race_black <- lm(bwt ~ race, data = birthwt_black_ref)
summary(mod_race_black)
```

</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 8</div>
  <p>With black as reference, the coefficient on <code>racewhite</code> is about +383 g. This means:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p7" value="a">White babies weigh about 383 g more than black babies, on average.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p7" value="b">White babies weigh 383 g in total.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p7" value="c">The race difference disappeared after releveling.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Same underlying gap, new reference: white vs black instead of black vs white." data-incorrect="Not quite. Releveling relabels comparisons; it does not change the data or erase differences."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="c">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 9</div>
  <p>With black as reference, the intercept (about 2720 g) represents:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p8" value="a">The grand mean across all races.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p8" value="b">The white group mean.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p8" value="c">The black group mean.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. The intercept always tracks the reference group." data-incorrect="Not quite. After releveling, black is reference, so the intercept is the black mean."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Exercise 1: fill in the education model (<code>prevend.samp</code>)</h2>

Replace each `____` to build the factor, set primary as the first level, and fit the model.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code — exercise 1 (fill in blanks)</h3>

```{webr-r}
library(oibiostat)
data(prevend.samp)

prevend <- prevend.samp
prevend$education <- factor(
  ____,
  levels = ____,
  labels = c("primary", "lower_secondary", "higher_secondary", "university")
)

mod_fill <- lm(____ ~ ____, data = prevend)
summary(mod_fill)
```

</div>

<details class="answer">
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

```r

prevend$education <- factor(

  levels = 0:3,

mod_fill <- lm(RFFT ~ education, data = prevend)
```

</details>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Exercise 2: three-level genotype predictor (<code>oibiostat::famuss</code>)</h2>

The FAMuSS study measured percent change in non-dominant arm strength (<code>ndrm.ch</code>) after resistance training, by ACTN3 genotype (<code>actn3.r577x</code>: CC, CT, or TT). Fill in the blanks and run the cell.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code — exercise 2 (fill in blanks)</h3>

```{webr-r}
library(oibiostat)
data(famuss)

mod_actn3 <- lm(____ ~ ____, data = famuss)
summary(mod_actn3)
```

</div>

<details class="answer">
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

```r
mod_actn3 <- lm(ndrm.ch ~ actn3.r577x, data = famuss)
```

With CC as the default reference, the intercept is the mean change for CC genotype. Each other row is the difference vs CC.

</details>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 11</div>
  <p>In the FAMuSS model, how many genotype coefficients appear below the intercept (excluding the intercept itself)?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p10" value="a">2 (for CT and TT; CC is reference).</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p10" value="b">3 (one per genotype).</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p10" value="c">1 (genotype is binary).</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Three levels → two dummy variables (K − 1)." data-incorrect="Not quite. With K = 3 levels, expect K − 1 = 2 slope rows."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 12</div>
  <p>The TT coefficient (about +9.2) tells you that TT participants' mean strength gain is about 9.2 percentage points:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p11" value="a">In total, regardless of genotype.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p11" value="b">Higher than the CC reference group.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p11" value="c">Higher than the CT group specifically.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Each dummy compares its level to the reference (CC), not to another non-reference level." data-incorrect="Not quite. The TT row is TT vs CC (reference), not TT vs CT."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel completion">

<h2>Completion code</h2>

<p>Answer at least 10 out of 12 questions correctly to reveal your completion code.</p>

<p><span class="code-progress" id="code-progress">0 of 12 correct (need at least 10)</span></p>

<div class="code-box" id="code-box">
  <div class="code-label">Your completion code</div>
  <div class="code-value" id="code-value"></div>
</div>

</section>

<p class="footer-note">GRAPH Courses practical | Polytomous categorical predictors</p>

</div>

<script>
const COMPLETION_CODE = "POLYKM1";
const COMPLETION_REQUIRED = 10;

function updateCompletion() {
  const cards = document.querySelectorAll(".practice");
  const correct = document.querySelectorAll(".practice.is-correct").length;
  const total = cards.length;
  const progress = document.getElementById("code-progress");
  const box = document.getElementById("code-box");
  const value = document.getElementById("code-value");

  if (progress) {
    progress.textContent = correct + " of " + total + " correct (need at least " + COMPLETION_REQUIRED + ")";
  }

  if (box && value) {
    if (correct >= COMPLETION_REQUIRED) {
      value.textContent = COMPLETION_CODE;
      box.style.display = "block";
    } else {
      box.style.display = "none";
    }
  }
}

document.querySelectorAll(".practice").forEach((card) => {
  const button = card.querySelector("button");
  const feedback = card.querySelector(".practice-feedback");
  const answer = card.dataset.answer;

  button.addEventListener("click", () => {
    const selected = card.querySelector("input[type='radio']:checked");
    card.classList.remove("is-correct", "is-incorrect");
    card.querySelectorAll("label").forEach((label) => {
      label.classList.remove("correct-choice", "incorrect-choice");
    });

    if (!selected) {
      card.classList.add("is-incorrect");
      feedback.textContent = "Choose an answer first, then check it.";
      updateCompletion();
      return;
    }

    const selectedLabel = selected.closest("label");
    const correctInput = card.querySelector(`input[value="${answer}"]`);
    const correctLabel = correctInput ? correctInput.closest("label") : null;

    if (selected.value === answer) {
      card.classList.add("is-correct");
      selectedLabel.classList.add("correct-choice");
      feedback.textContent = feedback.dataset.correct;
    } else {
      card.classList.add("is-incorrect");
      selectedLabel.classList.add("incorrect-choice");
      if (correctLabel) correctLabel.classList.add("correct-choice");
      feedback.textContent = feedback.dataset.incorrect;
    }

    updateCompletion();
  });
});

updateCompletion();
</script>
